decks.name: LeetCode #51 - N-Queens
decks.description: Place N queens on NxN chessboard so no two queens attack each other using backtracking

cards.question: N-Queens: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Given an integer n, return all distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle. You may return the answer in any order. Each solution contains a distinct board configuration of the n-queens' placement, where 'Q' and '.' both indicate a queen and an empty space, respectively.

solutions.name: Backtracking
solutions.explanation: Use backtracking to place queens row by row. Create board with all dots. For each row, try placing queen in each column and check if position is safe using helper function. Helper checks column above, left diagonal, and right diagonal for existing queens. If safe, place queen, recurse to next row, then backtrack by removing queen. When all rows filled, add board configuration to result. O(n!) time complexity as explores valid placements with pruning.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Hash Set)
solutions.explanation: Optimize safety checking using hash sets to track occupied columns and diagonals in O(1) time. Use three sets: col for columns, posDiag for positive diagonals (r+c is constant), negDiag for negative diagonals (r-c is constant). Before placing queen, check if column or either diagonal is occupied. After placing, add to all three sets. Backtrack by removing from sets and clearing board position. Much faster than iterating to check safety. Same O(n!) time but with better constant factors.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Visited Array)
solutions.explanation: Use boolean arrays instead of sets for tracking. Three arrays: col for n columns, posDiag for 2n-1 positive diagonals (r+c from 0 to 2n-2), negDiag for 2n-1 negative diagonals (r-c from -(n-1) to n-1, offset by n). Arrays provide O(1) access like sets but with better cache locality. For negDiag, add n to index to avoid negative indices (r-c+n). Mark true when occupied, false when backtracking. Same O(n!) time with array access patterns.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Bit Mask)
solutions.explanation: Most space-efficient solution using bit manipulation. Use three integers as bit masks: col for columns, posDiag for positive diagonals, negDiag for negative diagonals. Each bit represents whether position is occupied. Check conflict with bitwise AND: if (col & (1<<c)) checks if bit c is set. Toggle bits with XOR: col ^= (1<<c) both sets and clears bit. Works well for n≤15 (integer bit limit). Same O(n!) time with minimal space overhead and fast bitwise operations.
